claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess this, I'll need to gather some information about your situation and any children you're responsible for.

Let me start with a few questions:

**How many children are you seeking Child Benefit for?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! I'm looking to claim Child Benefit for one child - my son Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I'm now going to ask you some questions to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for your son, Alex.

**How old is Alex?**

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Since Alex is 18, I need to understand his current situation to determine eligibility.

**Is Alex currently in approved education or training (such as university, college, school, or an apprenticeship)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not in any education or training at the moment. He finished school and decided not to continue with further studies.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. I need to ask one more important question:

**Is Alex currently in paid work, and if so, how many hours per week is he working?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he works full-time at the supermarket.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I now have enough details to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Based on the information you've provided:

- Alex is 18 years old
- He is not in approved education or training
- He is working full-time

According to Child Benefit rules, you normally qualify for Child Benefit if your child is under 20 and they stay in approved education or training. However, once a child reaches 16 and is no longer in approved education or training, Child Benefit typically stops.

Additionally, Child Benefit ceases if your child starts paid work for 24 hours or more a week and is no longer in approved education or training.

Since Alex is 18, working full-time (which means more than 24 hours per week), and is not in approved education or training, you would **not be eligible** for Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'm sorry to inform you that you are **not eligible** for Child Benefit for Alex. 

The key reason is that while Child Benefit can normally continue for children under 20 if they remain in approved education or training, once they leave education and start working 24 hours or more per week, eligibility ends. Alex meets both of these conditions - he's no longer in education or training and is working full-time.

Is there anything else I can help you with?
